propositions: Write-op input surfaces (force, reason, caused_by, ref, close_class) are hand-mirrored across lib/CLI/MCP adapters with no mechanical guard against drift; gaps are caught only by chance or LLM review.

A transport-agnostic contract table (write_parity_contract.py) drives test execution of each case through all three adapters against a fresh temp store, classifying outcomes as ACCEPTED/REJECTED(rule)/PARAM_NOT_EXPOSED and failing the suite on any divergence between adapters.

Runtime conditional rules (close_class required for bug-close, reason required for REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES) are asserted behaviorally on every adapter; adapter-bound internals (source, return_alias, _creation_channel, repo_root) are excluded from the contract to prevent false divergences.

MCP gaps on reason/caused_by/force for transition and claim are encoded as strict-xfail rows citing scratchy-leprous-galago, keeping the suite green in CI while forcing removal of markers when the gaps close.
An in-suite simulated-parity fixture (_ConvergedMcpAdapter) proves the oracle detects convergence by flipping a strict-xfail row to xpass, validating the oracle's ability to enforce cleanup.
